**Test image analysis:**
- Tomato plant with collapsed/dead stem showing a distinct tan-brown canker/lesion
- Extensive wilting and browning of leaves (plant largely dead)
- Stem appears girdled at a point with some greenish coating
- Brown dead foliage throughout, with some green tissue remaining nearby
- Black plastic mulch visible at base

Key candidates: Southern_Blight (stem girdle at soil line, rapid collapse), Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (stem canker, white mycelium), Phytophthora_Blight (dark stem lesions, collapse)

Using my 1 reference view on the most likely candidate — Southern_Blight:

**Comparison:**
The Southern_Blight reference shows prominent white mycelial fan at the stem base with extensive root involvement. This does NOT match the test image well — the test image lacks the characteristic white mycelium fan.

**Revised analysis of test image:**
- Tan/brown bleached stem canker causing plant collapse — classic Sclerotinia appearance
- Extensive plant death/wilting
- No visible white mycelium fan at soil line (rules against Southern Blight)
- The stem's tan/bleached coloration and girdling lesion pattern points to **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**

Sclerotinia causes tan/bleached stem lesions, hollow stem (with sclerotia inside), and rapid plant death — matching the test image well.

Sclerotinia causes bleached stem tissue, hollow stem with sclerotia, and rapid plant collapse, matching the observed pattern."}
